findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State which `completion_expectation` value the config-unreadable/fail-open close (gates.py:79-87) records, or add a distinct value for it, so it is not silently folded into `gate_off`
evidence: Problem: 'config unreadable -> gate_enabled fails OPEN (_commands/gates.py:79-87)'
Direction enum values: required, gate_off, force_bypassed, local_source, not_certifiable, not_applicable — none names the fail-open case
findings.finding: The Problem section lists 'config unreadable -> gate_enabled fails OPEN (gates.py:79-87)' as one of the states that today collapse into 'closed with no attestation,' but the Direction enum provides no value for it. A fail-open close would presumably record `gate_off`, silently re-conflating a config-read failure with a genuine operator gate-off — the exact conflation this ticket exists to break.
findings.location: Problem section (fail-open bullet) vs Direction enum table
scenarios: Config becomes unreadable at close time; gate_enabled returns True/fails open; ticket closes with no attestation; a later reader sees `gate_off` and believes the operator deliberately disabled the gate
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `gate_unreadable` (or similarly named) enum value for the fail-open branch, OR explicitly document that fail-open records `gate_off` with a stated rationale that the reader accepts the conflation.

findings.checklist_item: Enumerate reducer/_processors.py (the _fold_close_class / STATUS-fold site) and schemas/ticket_state.schema.json as required edit targets, mirroring the close_class precedent, so completion_expectation reaches reduced state and AC-2's 'reading only reduced state' is achievable.
evidence: close_class becomes reduced state via three sites: written in txn.py:287-288, folded by _fold_close_class (reducer/_processors.py:203-217, invoked at :274 and :301), and declared in schemas/ticket_state.schema.json:187-190
AC-2: 'reading only reduced state, separates closed-and-signed ... from ... closed-with-gate-off'
Plan quote: 'Event-schema addition: STATUS field, reducer handling, and docs/event-schema.md' — names docs/event-schema.md but not reducer/_processors.py or ticket_state.schema.json
findings.finding: The plan's AC-2 requires a reader to separate the three states 'reading only reduced state,' but the reducer fold site (reducer/_processors.py _fold_close_class / the STATUS processor at lines 274,301) and the reduced-state schema (schemas/ticket_state.schema.json, where close_class is registered at :187-190) are not enumerated as edit targets. The plan invokes close_class as its precedent and names only the txn.py STATUS-data write; it says 'reducer handling' generically without naming reducer/_processors.py, and the event-schema addition line lists docs/event-schema.md but not ticket_state.schema.json. Without folding into compiled state and registering it in ticket_state.schema.json, completion_expectation would not be readable from reduced state, which is exactly what AC-2 demands.
findings.location: Direction section ('reducer handling'; 'writes it into the STATUS event data next to the present-only close_class') and Event-schema addition line; AC-2
scenarios: Implementer writes completion_expectation into STATUS data and updates docs/event-schema.md but never folds it in the reducer or registers it in ticket_state.schema.json; the field never reaches compiled state and AC-2's reduced-state read fails
findings.suggested_fix: In the Direction / event-schema-addition bullet, name the concrete fold site (reducer/_processors.py, alongside _fold_close_class) and add schemas/ticket_state.schema.json (register completion_expectation as reduced state, present-only) to the edit set, so the field is compiled into state and readable exactly as close_class is.

findings.location: Direction section, enum table (values `required`..`not_applicable`); AC-2 derivation table

findings.finding: The recorded 'expectation' derives from gate_enabled(), which fails OPEN (returns False) on unreadable config, so a config-unreadable close records 'not expected' and remains indistinguishable from a genuine gate-off close — a state the Problem section explicitly lists as collapsed but the solution does not resolve.
findings.suggested_fix: Either derive the expectation from a signal that separates fail-open-unreadable from configured-off (e.g. record the resolution outcome, not just the boolean), or amend the Problem/AC to state config-unreadable remains conflated with gate-off and why that is acceptable.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The Direction specifies recording 'the EXPECTATION and its outcome' as 'a field on the STATUS event' (singular), but the acceptance criteria demand a multi-way discriminator that a single boolean cannot express: AC2 must separate signed / signature-lost / gate-off, and AC3 additionally requires --force, local-source, and certifiable-false closes to NOT read as gate-off. Since all of gate-off, force, local-source, certifiable-false, and dropped-sidecar currently collapse into 'closed with no attestation', a boolean 'was a signature expected' distinguishes gate-off from the rest but leaves force/local/certifiable-false indistinguishable from a genuine signature-lost close. The plan does not enumerate the field's value vocabulary (bool vs enum, and which value each of the six enumerated close paths writes).
findings.location: Direction paragraph ('Record the EXPECTATION and its outcome ... field on the STATUS event') vs Acceptance criteria AC2/AC3
findings.suggested_fix: Define an enum-valued field (e.g. `completion_expectation` with values like `not_required`, `forced`, `local_unattested`, `withheld`, `required`) plus reader logic that treats `required` + missing attestation as signature-lost; state the config-unreadable-fails-open case's value explicitly.

findings.finding: The plan does not specify how the 'a completion signature was expected' value is computed and threaded into transition_core; it is NOT the same as the precheck's verified_result (which is None for a --force close even though a signature was expected), and transition_core currently accepts force_close_reason yet silently discards it — so a naively-threaded expectation param risks being ignored or mis-derived.

The plan asserts the close STATUS event's present-only `close_class` is 'documented `docs/event-schema.md:47`', but event-schema.md line 47 describes the STATUS event without mentioning `close_class`, and the string `close_class` appears nowhere in event-schema.md (it is documented instead in docs/user-guide.md:131 and docs/ticket-model.md:61).
findings.location: Problem/Direction — 'The close STATUS event records only ... present-only `close_class` (`txn.py:277-296`; documented `docs/event-schema.md:47`)'
